newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera says would buy all of Tabaquiera.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera says would buy all of Tabaquiera.

text.p: Spanish tobacco firm Tabacalera on Wednesday said that if it was chosen to take a majority stake in Portugal's Tabaqueira it would buy the remainder of the firm before the current deadline of two years.

"Tabacalera has expressed its commitment to buying the remaining 35 percent (of Tabaqueira) ahead of time in the measure that the (Portuguese) government decides," a spokesman for the company told Reuters.
The current privatisation envisages the sale of 65 percent of Tabaqueira now with the remaining 35 percent to be sold within two years in tranches of 20 and 15 percent respectively.
A special jury evaluating bids to buy the Portugese state company has ranked first an offer by U.S. concern Philip Morris in alliance with the Jorge de Mello group.
The report, which will serve as a basis for the final cabinet decision on the winner, placed Tabacalera third behind French company Seita despite the fact that it had offered the highest price.
The Tabacalera spokesman said the decision to award the majority stake could be taken at the next meeting of the Portuguese cabinet on Thursday. But he added there was no deadline for the decision.

Spanish government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez said Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar had not discussed the privatisation of Tabaqueira with his Portuguese counterpart at a bilateral summit on Wednesday.

Tabacelera recovered from a year low of 4,600 it set on Tuesday to trade up 100 pesetas at 4,700 at 1200 GMT. The share has lost 7.4 percent since the announcement on Friday that Philip Morris was in pole position for the privatisation.
